source.prompt: One original unbranded basketball, isolated centered object filling 80 percent of a square image on a plain light gray background. Early-2000s PlayStation 2 basketball game prop art, visibly low-poly spherical silhouette with about sixteen segments around circumference. Worn warm burnt-orange leather, broad baked-looking ochre and amber tonal variation, subtle scuffed mottling, deliberately limited 256-pixel texture appearance. Bold continuous dark brown-black basketball channels, clearly readable at a small gameplay size: equatorial seam, perpendicular great-circle seam and paired curved panel seams, clean regular panel structure. Flat broad shading with a gentle upper-left highlight, no tiny photoreal pores, no glossy reflections. Entire sphere visible, three-quarter view, no floor, no cast shadow, no hoop, no player, no extra balls. No text, numbers, manufacturer marks, league marks, logos, labels, watermarks or branding.

settings.meshAuthoring: Local indexed UV sphere, 16 longitude segments and 12 latitude segments, 0.12 meter radius

rejectedMeshAttempt.outcome: Rejected before job creation: free plan team custom-generation limit 50 CU, actionValue 19. User approved local mesh alternative.

optimizationSteps: Generated one original, unbranded concept through Scenario Gemini 3.1 Lite. User reference photos informed the art direction only; no third-party pixels were used.

After Scenario rejected the Tripo 3.1 request, the user explicitly chose a local low-poly mesh using the generated concept colors and wear. There is no generated Scenario 3D asset or successful 3D job.

Sampled an unmarked leather patch from the concept, resized it to 128x64, mirrored it across a 256x256 spherical color map, applied orange tint and broad tonal variation, and baked continuous dark equatorial and curved meridian channels into the map.

Exported an indexed 16x12 UV sphere with 352 nondegenerate outward-facing triangles, radial unit normals, flipped glTF V coordinates, Y-up meter coordinates, identity node transforms, and a centered pivot.

Embedded one optimized palette PNG with 128 colors into GLB; one rough material reuses the same color map for a modest emissive contribution so orange and dark seams remain visible under the existing arena lights. No normal/metalness/roughness texture, rig, animation, external image dependency, or decoder extension.
Validated the shipped binary with gltf-validator and direct geometry/texture measurements before release.
source.outputNotes: Hybrid asset: Scenario concept-derived leather texture and locally authored topology/channel pattern. Concept is filed in TheArena collection col_rgcLMCsPgwXnr25W3vjnkpNi. Raw concept, intermediates, rejected attempts, and test harness remain in ignored .tmp/ball and are not committed.

source.prompt: Original fictional early-2000s console basketball arena shell: broad charcoal and cool-purple walls, open tiered bleachers, chunky exposed ceiling lattice, warm court-facing light housings, restrained amber edges, four fictional venue video boards and an offset red 24 shot clock. Preserve the existing 15.2 by 14 meter wood court, hoop and lighting landmarks; avoid logos, copied signage and unnecessary buried faces.
source.negativePrompt: No real team, league, sponsor, player likeness, copied sign, photo texture, high-frequency detail, or hidden solid seating blocks.

settings.method: Deterministic local mesh and SVG atlas authoring; custom indexed glTF 2.0 binary writer

optimizationSteps: Authored exposed wall, ceiling, foundation, step and truss faces in meter-scale world coordinates; omitted buried bleacher bottoms and wall backs.
Batched the shell into 20 named meshes and 10 shared materials, with one 512-square PNG atlas for fictional video-board graphics.
Used one 24-triangle local seat mesh for 240 runtime instances; retained the established instanced crowd and four existing spotlight references.
Kept the procedural shell visible during loading and on missing or invalid GLB; disposed its geometry after the authored shell passed runtime validation.
Verified the optimized GLB binary, accessor bounds, triangle areas, unit normals, UV range and identity node transforms independently of the generator.
source.outputNotes: Original local primitives and SVG lettering. Five user-provided game screenshots informed broad PS2-era seating and architectural direction only; no reference pixels, names, branding or geometry were copied. The generator is committed for reproducibility; no raw image generations or large intermediates are committed.

license.name: Original locally authored TheArena asset
license.evidence: Mesh recipe, layout, material palette and atlas artwork were authored for this repository from geometric primitives and SVG. User-supplied screenshots served as style references only; the runtime files contain no third-party pixels, marks or copied signage.

validation.notes: Desktop start and gameplay views, forward keyboard movement and court-marking visibility were inspected locally. Portrait and landscape narrow viewports kept the hoop, clock and key in frame; this browser reports a fine pointer, so these are viewport checks rather than physical touch-device or touch-control performance tests. The four-board material retains the exact arena video board name used by main.js for its emissive pulse. With the GLB temporarily absent, the original shell remained visible; restoring it loaded the authored shell. The existing court, hoop, player, camera, controls, physics, lights and gameplay audio were not edited. Shell walls face inward so an outside camera sees through their back faces at extreme court positions. Mobile memory and draw-call checks use shipped geometry/bytes; physical-device FPS remains unmeasured.

integration.fallback: The complete original procedural shell, bleachers, boards and shot clock remain visible during loading and on network, decode or mesh-validation failure; successful GLB loading removes and disposes their geometry.
